newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH NICHE FOOD GROUPS MAY REAP EMU GAINS - MTK.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH NICHE FOOD GROUPS MAY REAP EMU GAINS - MTK.

text.p: Big Finnish food industry groups with overseas operations and small firms capable of flexibility are best prepared to meet increasing competition from the third stage of EMU, a food sector marketing expert said on Tuesday.

"Big companies that have become internationalised, or ... small firms that can flexibly adjust to new conditions will survive best in the single currency area," MTK food production and marketing director Markku Suojanen told Reuters.
MTK -- the Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners -- is the farmers' lobby.
"It has been estimated that medium-sized businesses will have a difficult time finding their place," Suojanen said.
Bucking doomsday forecasts, the Finnish food industry has managed well in the European Union (EU) following Finland's accession in 1995 -- and foodstuffs exports have increased steadily, MTK said.
The trend in food and beverages companies' earnings was mixed last year, with half reporting profits up and half profits down on 1995.
Customs statistics for 1996 showed a 25 percent increase in the value of food and beverages exports.
Particularly exports of meat, dairy and grain products increased substantially.
But the food industry and raw material producers had applied a "dumping of prices policy" in order to increase their competitiveness, Suojanen said.
"This is not a lasting solution from the (agricultural) producers' point of view," he said.
According to MTK statistics, Finnish eggs and feeds are the cheapest in Europe.

"Producer prices should correlate with the price standards of the country -- food can not be the only item in Finland that is priced according to South European standards," MTK chairman Esa Harmala told a news conference on Monday.
Harmala said European economic and monetary union (EMU) will bring consolidation to the food industry and said there would be "clearly fewer players in the business by 2005".

One way to stand out in the new competive EMU environment was to develop niche products like Raision Tehtaat's cholesterol-reducing margarine Benecol and Cultor's birch sweetener xylitol, Suojanen said.
"Both Cultor and Raisio developed their new strategies already well before (Finland's) EU membership, which is an example to follow for firms preparing for EMU," he said.
